findings.summary: currentQuestion is assigned once before the while loop and never reassigned; the loop always processes the same question every iteration
findings.failure_scenario: gaps is initialized as ['what is...']. Line 273 shifts it out: currentQuestion='what is...', gaps=[]. Loop condition (line 274) is gaps.length > 0 || currentQuestion === question, which is 0>0 || true = always true. Inside the loop body, gaps may receive new sub-questions via reflect (e.g. ['who founded...', 'what is...']), but currentQuestion is never updated from gaps. Every iteration sends the same original question to the LLM. Sub-questions sit in gaps unprocessed forever. The only exits are the return statements in the answer handler (lines 342, 364). If the LLM never produces a passing answer, the loop runs until API quota is exhausted or the process is killed.

findings.summary: dedupQueries returns { unique_queries, tokens } but reflect handler assigns the full object to newGapQuestions (a string[]), so .length check always fails and sub-questions are never added
findings.failure_scenario: Agent takes 'reflect' action with questionsToAnswer=['sub-q1', 'sub-q2']. allQuestions.length is 1 (truthy), so line 422 executes: newGapQuestions = await dedupQueries(['sub-q1','sub-q2'], ['original-q']). dedupQueries returns object { unique_queries: ['sub-q1'], tokens: 42 }. newGapQuestions now holds this object. Line 424: newGapQuestions.length evaluates to undefined (objects lack numeric length). undefined > 0 is false. The else branch (lines 436-446) always executes, reporting 'you have asked them before.' The valid sub-question 'sub-q1' is silently discarded; it is never pushed to gaps or allQuestions. The agent cannot decompose complex questions into sub-questions.

findings.summary: tokenBudget loop guard removed without replacement; no upper bound on loop iterations or API token consumption
findings.failure_scenario: The old function signature getResponse(question, tokenBudget=1000000) provided a hard cap on total tokens consumed. Combined with finding 1 (infinite loop), the agent will make unlimited Gemini API calls until the process is killed, the API key is rate-limited, or the quota is exhausted. Even after fixing finding 1, there is no programmatic backstop preventing runaway costs from an unbounded reasoning loop.
